# Map transport / hardware repair — family beta

Scope: `agent/mobile-companion` only. No production deployment or release packaging.
Recovered application checkpoint: `173a32536560acb8a2fa24f5d2274aec120b023b`.
The prior rail removal, side-mounted housings, bottom sequence bracket, 2.8-second
uneven roll, worn splice, and V3 gearmotor assets are retained.

## Repaired causes

- The regional renderer hid its outgoing SVG immediately on airport selection,
  before transport could finish. Both map sheets now remain available during travel.
- Hidden-attribute writes conflated the desired map with the temporary visibility
  needed for transport. The airport controller now sends explicit desired-view
  requests; the latest request wins, including repeated live updates during a roll.
- Registration waits for both sheets and the splice, then two animation frames.
  Canceled transports and obsolete, still-downloading sounds cannot clack later.
- The no-chart diagnostic previously rolled into an empty aperture and snapped
  back. It now transports a second copy of the existing map and returns it; no
  airport geometry or live position is fabricated for this demonstration.
- Conflicting old inset/grid and typography rules defeated the bezel mounts.
  The hardware layer now fills the aperture. Housing size, font size, and mounts
  are measured from the map opening, not the browser window. The current-time arm
  reaches the left bezel, ETA reaches the right, and the sequence bracket reaches
  the bottom. No feet or full-width rail were added. Empty sequence housings are
  opaque; long sequence summaries wrap inside the housing.
- Compact mobile's independent 2.55-second controller has been replaced with a
  build of the shared transport/audio sources. Its cached legacy URL is only a loader.
- Reduced motion no longer loses to an inline duration override. Visible sheets
  never vertically overshoot registration; the approved lateral settling remains.

## Verification

The normal `npm test` command builds both browser bundles, checks ES5 syntax,
checks the existing application, and includes new visibility-request and delayed-
audio cancellation regressions. The branch-only `map-hardware-check.yml` workflow
also runs `scripts/map-hardware-browser-test.py`; its exact-SHA result is the
source of truth for the full run.

The browser proof uses real application markup/styles/source with local image
embedding and explicitly synthetic flight/airport fixtures. It never calls live
providers or uses family credentials. Eight geometry cases cover 1920/1366 desktop,
1024/768 full-family landscape/portrait, 390/320 compact phone, phone landscape,
and a deliberately forced full-panel phone view. It checks contained text,
non-overlapping housings, attached mounts, opaque housings, and page width.
Frame sampling verifies adjacent sheets and stationary hardware near the end of
travel, both directions, mid-roll resize, repeated view requests, unrelated
animation events, real-time diagnostic return, and reduced motion. Sound dispatch
is instrumented to prove registration follows visual cleanup; V3 audio assets
were not replaced or resynthesized.

This is headless Chromium verification, not a claim of hands-on validation on the
home PC or the older iPad. Full mode deliberately scales the whole physical panel;
on a narrow portrait phone, Compact remains the readable family layout. Final
sound balance and physical-device visual approval remain owner checks.

## Local installation boundary

Saving this branch does not update the running home server. Pull the branch,
install dependencies, rebuild the browser files, and restart the family-beta
server through the existing beta workflow before checking the physical display.
